PullRequest.Title: test: stabilize Codex shared-workspace startup on Linux
PullRequest.Body:
Codex 0.153.0 can fail to start concurrent chats in an empty shared workspace on Linux: bubblewrap reports that a protected metadata mount source no longer exists. This caused `CodexMaterializeFailed` in the server-tool tests exercised by #337659.

Create `.git`, `.agents`, and `.codex` before starting Codex in this suite's disposable Linux workspaces. This preserves all 39 existing scenario bodies and assertions, concurrency, permissions, timeouts, and recorded replay fixtures. The known-issues note tracks the remaining runtime defect and how to remove the workaround after an SDK fix.

### Platform scope

Reviewed public Codex source at `rust-v0.153.0`, commit `41e22fee981a63b3698df7ed36bad393cda24715`:

- [Linux sandbox modules](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.153.0/codex-rs/linux-sandbox/src/lib.rs#L6) compile bubblewrap and its cleanup only for Linux.
- [Readable mounts](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.153.0/codex-rs/linux-sandbox/src/bwrap.rs#L503) use paths observed during argument construction; [synthetic-target cleanup](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.153.0/codex-rs/linux-sandbox/src/linux_run_main.rs#L1093) removes temporary targets. [Existing target identities are preserved](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.153.0/codex-rs/linux-sandbox/src/bwrap.rs#L187), explaining the fixture workaround.
- [Backend selection](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.153.0/codex-rs/sandboxing/src/manager.rs#L62) uses Seatbelt on native macOS and the Windows sandbox on native Windows. [Seatbelt protects paths through policy rules](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.153.0/codex-rs/sandboxing/src/seatbelt.rs#L553); [Windows applies ACLs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.153.0/codex-rs/windows-sandbox-rs/src/workspace_acl.rs#L23). Neither uses the Linux temporary-mount cleanup.
- Scope follows the filesystem executor OS, not the UI OS: Linux execution environments, including remote Linux and WSL2, can still be affected. This does not claim that other platforms have no unrelated startup races.

### Larger local validation

| Experiment | Baseline failures / executions | Prepared-directory failures / executions |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Linux: four existing integration scenarios, completed 100-test worker batches | **5 / 1,600** | **0 / 1,600** |
| Linux: direct app-server concurrent thread starts | **65 / 2,000** | **0 / 2,000** |
| Native macOS: same integration scenarios without the workaround | **0 / 1,600** | Not applied on macOS |
| Native macOS: direct app-server concurrent thread starts | **0 / 2,000** | **0 / 2,000** |

The direct Linux baseline failures occurred in both baseline blocks: 33/1,000 and 32/1,000; both fixed blocks were 0/1,000. Every direct Linux failure and all five failures in the completed Linux integration batches had the exact missing protected-metadata mount error.

Interpretation: this supports the fixture mitigation and the Linux-specific mechanism much more strongly than the earlier 1/160 sample, but does not prove a zero failure rate. Under an independent-trial model, 0/1,600 gives a one-sided 95% upper bound of approximately 0.19%; 0/2,000 gives approximately 0.15%. Trials share runtime state and scheduling, so those are illustrative bounds, not product reliability guarantees. The integration comparison alone is still sparse (two-sided Fisher exact p ≈ 0.062 under the independence assumption); the separate direct-start reproduction and release-source analysis provide additional evidence.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction method, environment, and interrupted attempts</summary>

The four integration scenarios were:
- `list_sessions can include an archived session on request`
- `list_sessions hides archived sessions by default`
- `list_sessions includeArchived returns active and archived sessions`
- `list_sessions status filter combines active and archived sessions`

Each worker registered those same test bodies 25 times under their original titles in an untracked compiled copy, preserving per-test setup/teardown, normal lease recycling, strict replay, and fixture selection. Four isolated runner processes ran per block; baseline/fixed blocks alternated in a balanced order. Baseline removed only the seven-line protected-directory setup. No production code, test bodies, timeouts, or model fixtures were changed for the experiment.

Selected tests run with:

```sh
./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/providers/codexAgentHostE2E.integrationTest.ts --grep 'server tool: list_sessions (can include an archived session on request|hides archived sessions by default|includeArchived returns active and archived sessions|status filter combines active and archived sessions)'
```

Linux used local Ubuntu 24.04 Docker, bubblewrap 0.9.0, CI-built x64 dependencies and Electron 43.7.3, with published **ARM64 Codex 0.153.0 running natively** on the ARM64 host. The x64 Codex binary cannot install seccomp under emulation. Codex sandboxing stayed enabled. Electron required `--no-sandbox` for the root container. Native macOS used the published Darwin ARM64 Codex 0.153.0 binary. No local Windows stress run was available.

The direct experiment ran the published app-server over stdio, initialized its experimental API, and sent pairs of concurrent `thread/start` requests into fresh empty workspaces using VS Code's unchanged platform permission profiles. Each condition had 1,000 pairs (2,000 starts), in baseline/fixed/fixed/baseline blocks. Only the directory precreation differed. Successful threads were unsubscribed after each pair; no model turns, credentials, or external model calls were needed.

**Interrupted attempts are not hidden in the denominators:** one initial Linux runner failed before executing tests because four runners raced to create their shared crash-report directory. Later, a long-lived container without an init process accumulated 21,968 zombie processes and several stress runs timed out or were interrupted. Those partial baseline runs logged **254 passing test events, 4 failed test events, and 4 hook failures**, outside the completed-worker comparison above; they included additional matching mount failures. The environment was restarted with Docker `--init`, and replacement batches completed the 1,600-per-condition comparison. In that clean environment, an additional baseline block reproduced the exact race (1/400), while the matching fixed block passed (0/400). This mixed-environment sample should not be treated as a precisely controlled estimate of the CI failure rate.

</details>

Other validation:
- `npm run compile-client` and precommit hygiene passed.
- Normal `--grep 'server tool:'` replay: **39 passed on Linux and 39 passed on macOS**.
- [Azure build 477773](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=477773) **succeeded**, including Linux, macOS, and Windows Electron tests, on the fixture-change commit `0df6b496e8f`; the follow-up commit only documents platform scope.
- GitHub's Linux and macOS Electron jobs passed on that commit. The Windows Codex E2E suite also passed; its job timed out later in unrelated extension tests.

Scenarios.Scenario: Codex server-tools E2E test session startup on Linux
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For each enabled test, a temporary workspace is created, then the diff synchronously creates `.git`, `.agents`, and `.codex`; only after those three local filesystem operations complete does `createRealSession`/`createSession` IPC initialize the provider-backed session. The new work is on test setup's critical path but not any product runtime path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create a unique temporary workspace directory
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One `mkdtempSync` per server-tools scenario, up to the suite's 39 existing scenario bodies.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The suite already synchronously created one fresh temporary workspace per scenario.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before session creation; unchanged by the diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create three empty protected metadata directories
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly three `mkdirSync` calls per fresh workspace, only when provider is Codex and the executor OS is Linux; at the full 39-scenario suite size this is 117 bounded local metadata operations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No protected metadata directories were precreated, so there were zero corresponding mkdir calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Completes before provider session startup; this is introduced setup work, but it is constant per test and tiny relative to the existing provider startup/turn boundaries.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Initialize/authenticate/create and subscribe to an Agent Host provider session
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One primary session creation per scenario, with a small fixed number of additional sessions in scenarios that exercise peer sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same session initialization and provider process path ran immediately after temporary workspace creation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This pre-existing IPC/provider startup dominates progress after workspace setup; the diff neither adds calls nor increases their cardinality or concurrency.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Recursively remove tracked temporary workspaces at suite teardown
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One recursive removal per tracked workspace; the three new entries are empty directories inside each already-tracked workspace, not additional cleanup roots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same workspace root was already recursively removed, with three fewer empty entries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occurs at suite teardown after scenarios complete; adds only three empty directory entries per Codex/Linux workspace to existing recursive cleanup.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of enabled Codex/Linux server-tools scenarios; effective added cardinality is fixed at three local directory creations per unique test workspace, with no input-sized loop or shared-workspace multiplication.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The directory loop is synchronous and serial. Mocha executes tests within the suite serially by default; provider subprocesses are reused/recycled by the existing lease, and the diff does not launch work concurrently or alter server/session concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Every scenario intentionally uses a new `mkdtemp` workspace, so there is no application cache or reusable cache key. Cold and warm runs both perform the same three creates; directories live only for the suite and are removed by existing teardown. There is no negative-cache or coalescing behavior to change.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed loop, platform/provider guard, session call ordering, caller count, serial execution model, and cleanup owner are directly visible in the traced code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact filesystem latency varies by CI host, but the cardinality and lifecycle are fully bounded and the operations create empty local directories. Any added duration is test-only and negligible compared with existing provider startup and model/replay work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The PR adds bounded test-fixture filesystem setup to prevent failed Codex/Linux starts; it does not affect product runtime, increase expensive session boundary calls, create a concurrency burst, or retain resources beyond existing teardown.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The Markdown addition is static repository documentation and executes no application or test runtime code.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Not applicable; no runtime cache is touched.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed hunk contains documentation only.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance mechanism or reportable regression.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete two-file diff and traced the test workspace setup through session IPC/provider startup and suite teardown. The sole runtime change adds three guarded, synchronous empty-directory creates per fresh Codex/Linux test workspace. This is bounded test-only work, does not alter expensive boundary cardinality or concurrency, and is cleaned by existing lifecycle ownership; no performance finding is warranted.
